name: Karen M. Feigh
title: David S. Lewis Professor and Associate Chair for Research
department: Daniel Guggenheim School of Aerospace Engineering; courtesy School of Interactive Computing
fitReason: Strong CS-method overlap in explicit belief representations, multimodal robot perception and proactive human-AI collaboration. Much of the broader aviation work uses simulation, so the specific physical household-robot line should anchor a project discussion.

physicalEvidence.summary: The April 2026 arXiv release of Inferring World Belief States in Dynamic Real-World Environments explicitly reports deployment on a Stretch RE2 to maintain a semantic map and infer a person’s belief state. Its stack uses OWLv2, SAM2, RTMPose and MMPose. Quantitative belief-state and Qwen/deBERTa active-assistance evaluations are in VirtualHome; the physical extension is qualitative with acknowledged hardware limitations. No physical manipulation, quantitative real-human belief accuracy or closed-loop learned navigation is established. First author Jack Kolb confirms Feigh was his PhD adviser, but graduated in May 2025 and now works at Apple; current platform/mentoring availability needs checking.

shortVisit.summary: No current public external-master’s short-visit or summer internship invitation was verified. Faculty-directory visitor-resource links concern campus logistics, not research appointments. Lab-page fetches failed, so no conclusions about current intake are drawn from their absence.

scoreReasons.fit: 38/40: close belief modeling, foundation-model perception and physically grounded human-AI collaboration.
scoreReasons.physical: 20/25: real Stretch extension explicitly reported, but qualitative and tied to a now-former advisee; current independent platform access not confirmed.
scoreReasons.freshness: 15/15: substantive primary preprint released April 2026; this is source freshness, not a claim that the hardware experiment occurred in 2026.
